properties.citation: G. P. Murdock, Africa: Its Peoples and Their Culture History, McGraw-Hill, 1959, « Tribal Map of Africa »; polygons digitised by Nathan Nunn (https://scholar.harvard.edu/nunn/pages/data-0, murdock_shapefile.zip); copy used: https://github.com/sboysel/murdock/blob/master/data-raw/Murdock_EA_2011_vkZ.geojson. Murdock's polygons ASHANTI, AKYEM and BRONG, as a proxy for the Twi-speaking groups (Asante, Akyem, Akuapem, Kwahu, Bono).
properties.derivation: Built by social/video/areas.mjs: the research's polygon yk-twi.geojson, kept inside the Natural Earth 1:50m polygon of Ghana (ADM0_A3 GHA) so its outer edge is the country's; on a 0.05° grid (cells whose centre falls inside), traced back as the cell boundary, simplified by Douglas–Peucker at 0.05° and rounded to 0.01°; parts and holes under 5000 km² dropped. The weakest of the four: Murdock has no polygon for Twi as a language, and his ASHANTI reaches the coast at Cape Three Points, so the area also covers the Ahanta and Wassa coast. His names are the colonial ethnonyms of 1959.
